design_note: Separates transport redelivery from business correlation through four explicit ingestion outcomes. Repeated delivery repairs its original work, while a new alert can attach to an existing incident.

source.title: Amazon SQS at-least-once delivery
source.concept: At-least-once message delivery can repeat an already received event. Consumers need idempotent processing so repetition does not create unintended additional work.
source.scope: Original event-ID and incident-correlation decisions. The source supports redelivery handling; the fictional application owns correlation and durable workflow dispatch.

lesson.title: A new delivery is not always a new incident
lesson.intro: AegisOps receives valid, tenant-scoped alerts with stable source event IDs. A deterministic correlation rule has complete inputs. First decide whether the delivery repeats an event already durably recorded.

data.root: Valid alert: look up source + event ID

yes.label: YES: attach new event to that incident

read: A repeated transport ID keeps its original durable ownership.
A missing workflow start needs repair rather than a second incident.
A different event can share an incident when the stated correlation rule matches.
lesson.question: If a correlation window changes overnight, should a redelivered stored event become a new incident?
lesson.answer: No. Its stable source-plus-event identity still resolves to the original ingestion record. Repair any unfinished dispatch under that identity. Correlation controls how distinct events are grouped; it must not erase transport deduplication. Neither a managed queue nor successful workflow start grants authority for a production change.
lesson.takeaway: Deduplicate delivery by stable event identity; correlate distinct events by the declared business rule.
lesson.assumption: Fictional valid events; identity lookup and new ownership are atomic, durable dispatch is recoverable, and correlation yields a definite decision.
